TX-2025892-SB12.aiSummary: The bill gives the Texas attorney general the power to prosecute crimes under state election laws and to represent the state in those cases. It also requires law enforcement and local prosecutors to share reports and other information about those cases with the attorney general. The law applies only to offenses committed on or after its effective date, which is the 91st day after the last day of the legislative session.

TX-2025892-SB54.aiSummary: The law changes how voters can be accepted when their home address is no longer current because they moved within the same county. It also says some voter registration updates tied to change-of-address notices take effect right away, instead of waiting 30 days. The changes apply only to change-of-address notices sent on or after the law’s effective date.

TX-2025892-HB26.aiSummary: The law lets sheriffs and constables in counties with more than 3.3 million people make contracts to provide law enforcement services for local governments, property owners' groups, or landowners. The county government could not block or change those contracts, and the sheriff or constable would set the terms. It was signed by the governor and takes effect on the 91st day after the last day of the legislative session.

TX-2025892-HB20.aiSummary: The law creates a state program for local governments to name a nonprofit or financial institution that can take disaster relief donations during a declared disaster, and it also requires local websites to share that information and tips on avoiding scams. It creates new crimes for dishonest disaster fundraising and for taking disaster-related property, and it raises the punishment in some cases. It also lets donors or donees sue for 300% of the money taken, plus lawyer fees, and it takes effect 91 days after the legislative session ends.

TX-2025892-HB192.title: Relating to the funding of law enforcement agencies in certain counties.

actions.text: Statement(s) of vote recorded in Journal
Reason for vote recorded in Journal
Comte report filed with Committee Coordinator

TX-2025892-HB192.policyArea: COMPTROLLER OF PUBLIC ACCOUNTS (V2608), CONSTABLES (S2357), City Government--Employees/Officers (I0061)

votes.motion: Senate Rule 7.18 and the Constitutional Rule requiring bills to be read on three several days be suspended and that HB 192 be placed on its third reading and final passage.

TX-2025892-HB192.aiSummary: The law applies to counties with more than 3.3 million people and limits when they can cut or move money from law enforcement budgets. It requires voter approval before a county can reduce or shift certain sheriff or constable funding, lets residents file a complaint if a county does this without approval, and gives the comptroller a role in checking it. If a county does not get the needed approval, it can face limits on its tax rate until the money is restored or voters approve the change. It took effect on the 91st day after the legislative session ended.

votes.motion: concur in the House amendment to SB 1.
Senate Rule 7.18 and the Constitutional Rule requiring bills to be read on three several days be suspended and that CSSB 1 be placed on its third reading and final passage.

TX-2025892-SB1.aiSummary: The law adds safety rules for campgrounds and youth camps in Texas, especially for places near flood areas. It requires campground cabins in floodplains to have roof access ladders and evacuation plans, and it bars or limits licenses for youth camps with cabins in floodplains. It also requires youth camps to keep emergency plans, train staff and campers, post evacuation routes, keep backup internet and weather alert systems, and share approved plans with parents and local emergency managers.
